evals.name: url-shortener-hash
evals.prompt: For a URL shortener handling 100M new links a day for 10 years, should the short key be a hash of the URL or a base-62 encoded ID? We also need click analytics.
evals.expected_output: Base-62 of a unique ID (7 chars covers 3.5 trillion) with a distributed ID generator, the guessability caveat, hash + collision resolution as the alternative, and 302 redirects because analytics are required, citing Vol. 1 ch. 8.
expectations: Computes or states that 7 base-62 characters give about 3.5 trillion keys, enough for 365 billion URLs.
Recommends base-62 conversion of a unique ID and names the need for an ID generator.
Mentions that sequential IDs are guessable.
Chooses 302 over 301 because click analytics are required.

evals.name: feed-fanout
evals.prompt: Our timeline precomputes every follower's feed on post. Celebrities with 2M followers are killing the workers. What do we change?
evals.expected_output: Keep fan-out on write for ordinary users, switch celebrities to fan-out on read (followers pull their posts at request time), cap feed cache length, store post IDs not objects, and use a queue with workers, citing Vol. 1 ch. 11.
expectations: Diagnoses the hotkey/celebrity problem of fan-out on write.
Recommends the hybrid approach: push for most users, pull for high-follower accounts.
Recommends storing post IDs (not full objects) in the feed cache with a length cap.
